name: kda_forward_k128_v128_bf16
description: Kimi Delta Attention packed-varlen forward with bf16 q/k/v/g/beta activations, fp32 gate parameters and per-sequence initial state, fused q/k L2 normalization, lower-bounded safe gate, beta sigmoid, and V-first recurrent-state layout. Candidates return both the bf16 output and the fp32 final recurrent state; both are scored. The six shapes match KDA-internal: 8192 total tokens, 96 or 64 heads, and fixed, mixed-varlen, or uniform-varlen sequence packing. The full benchmark scores each shape with standard and saturated gate inputs, for 12 cases; saturated inputs set A_log=log(16), dt_bias=0, and g=3. Beyond the timed cases the suite gates candidates on ten untimed stress probes at the operator's numerical edge, two probes checked against an fp64 token-by-token recurrence, and a salted private holdout.

batch_size.description: Packed-varlen input uses a single outer batch dimension.

total_tokens.description: Total tokens packed across all independent sequences.

num_heads.description: Query, key, value, and per-channel gate head count; workloads use 96 or 64.

num_seqs.description: Number of independently initialized sequences packed into total_tokens.

len_cu_seqlens.description: Zero for the single-sequence fixed case, otherwise num_seqs + 1.

gate_dim.description: Flattened per-head, per-key-channel gate bias dimension.

q.description: Raw queries; the kernel applies L2 normalization.

k.description: Raw keys; the kernel applies L2 normalization.

g.description: Raw per-key-channel gate logits before the lower-bounded safe-gate activation.

beta.description: Raw bf16 delta-update gate logits before sigmoid.

initial_state.description: Independent V-first recurrent state for each packed sequence.

cu_seqlens.description: Cumulative sequence offsets for packed varlen cases; None for one fixed-length sequence.

final_state.description: Per-sequence recurrent state after the last token of each packed sequence, in the same V-first layout as initial_state. Scored elementwise alongside output, so the state epilogue is part of every candidate's timed work.

reference:
import os

import torch

os.environ["FLA_FLASH_KDA"] = "0"
os.environ["FLA_TILELANG"] = "0"

from fla.ops.kda import chunk_kda


@torch.no_grad()
def run(q, k, v, g, beta, A_log, dt_bias, scale, initial_state, cu_seqlens=None):
    # The harness evaluates this oracle in the same process as the FlashKDA
    # baseline, which sets FLA_FLASH_KDA=1 on every call. Restore this oracle's
    # backend per call too, or the two interleave into the same implementation
    # and the comparison becomes a kernel checked against itself.
    os.environ["FLA_FLASH_KDA"] = "0"
    os.environ["FLA_TILELANG"] = "0"
    output, final_state = chunk_kda(
        q=q,
        k=k,
        v=v,
        g=g,
        beta=beta,
        scale=float(scale),
        use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=True,
        use_gate_in_kernel=True,
        use_beta_sigmoid_in_kernel=True,
        state_v_first=True,
        safe_gate=True,
        lower_bound=-5.0,
        A_log=A_log,
        dt_bias=dt_bias,
        initial_state=initial_state,
        output_final_state=True,
        cu_seqlens=cu_seqlens,
    )
    return output, final_state
